summary: The first lighthouse in the United States, lit in 1716 on Little Brewster Island; the tower dates from 1783 and was staffed until 2023.

access.note: The Park Service says the lighthouse and Little Brewster Island are not open to the public; summer lighthouse cruises view it from the water.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the story: first-tower cost (nomination and Heap: 2,385 pounds; Johnson: 2,285); date and number of burnings in 1775 (NPS 20 July, 31 July and September; nomination early July and 31 July; Heap 20 July and 31 July); explosion March 1776 (nomination) vs June 1776 (NPS); 1783 tower height 75 ft (NPS) vs 68 ft (Heap); heightening 1859 (nomination, NPS) vs 1860 (Heap's reprinted Transcript account); second keeper Saunders (USLHS, Lighthousefriends) vs Haynes (Heap); who asked for the 1719 cannon (nomination: the first keeper, who had drowned in 1718; Lighthousefriends: Hayes). NRHP listing: the Park Service says 1987; our record has 1966 (reference 66000133); not settled here. Light-dues 'Id.' in Johnson's OCR is read as one penny. Heap's account reprints a newspaper of 1880 and is second-hand for the colonial and Revolutionary details. 1921 Bulletin page is two columns interleaved in OCR: Hart/Howard and Small/second assistant were matched by position and text; the checker should read the page image. The 1924 Bulletin prints the first assistant as W. J. Howland where USLHS has William J. Howard. Fiscal-year reports: the 1892 and 1900 Light-House Board entries cover the year ended 30 June of those years; the 1894 appendix is read from the volume catalogued as 1893-94 (the title page before it reads fiscal 1894). The USLHS place record has latitude 40.33 (should be 42.33); the roster was matched by name, not position. Roster: all principal, assistant keepers and USCG names with start year up to 1959 are included; Coast Guard crew from 1960 on are left out (privacy rule). The USLHS typo 'Charles F. Stranger (189-1896)' is entered with no start year. The story calls Lighthousefriends' Tom Small and the archive's Thomas Small the same second assistant; the Bulletin does not name him. Today: the NPS page says the island is closed to the public; Lighthousefriends' visitor note (ranger-escorted tours, climbing) looks out of date. GSA gave a 60-day interest period from 3 August 2026 per Lighthousefriends; no recipient had been named in the sources read. Newspaper search (Chronicling America) found no usable page.
